title: Refine Playing Card Reveal
question: These three stay inside your reference's physical-card world: ivory textured stock, burgundy/black ink, restrained gold foil, natural light, and no digital effects. Pick the composition we should turn into the interactive Pass 2.0 beta.

options.label: Classic Border
options.lineage: bespoke casino stationery and traditional playing-card borders
options.thesis: A richly framed physical card that preserves the reference's identity while giving the QR its own clean, scan-safe lower register.
options.viewport: The complete card nearly fills a portrait phone screen, with the ornate border framing a centered information hierarchy and large QR bay.
options.risk: The patterned border is memorable, but it is also the busiest option and needs disciplined responsive scaling on very small phones.

options.label: Split Seal
options.lineage: modern private-club credentials and custom casino card decks
options.thesis: A narrow suit rail carries the casino identity so the main field can stay exceptionally clean, contemporary, and scan-focused.
options.viewport: A vertical burgundy rail stays visible at every size while the guest details and oversized QR occupy the quiet ivory field.
options.risk: The asymmetric structure is more distinctive digitally, though it moves furthest from the traditional framed reference.

options.label: Dealer's Register
options.lineage: casino table registers and restrained luxury invitation printing
options.thesis: The most minimal version treats event data like a precisely ruled register, leaving the largest possible uninterrupted QR zone.
options.viewport: Thin perimeter rules and corner indices frame a centered ledger of details, followed by the largest QR treatment of the set.
options.risk: It scans and scales best, but the quieter treatment may feel less like a special casino-night collectible.
